questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Triangle ABC has A(0, 0), B(2b, 0), and C(2c, 2d), with b ≠ 0 and d ≠ 0. Prove that the point G((2b + 2c)/3, 2d/3) lies on all three medians.
questions.prompt_markup: Triangle ABC has A(0, 0), B(2b, 0), and C(2c, 2d), with b ≠ 0 and d ≠ 0. Prove that the point G((2b + 2c)/3, 2d/3) lies on all three medians.
questions.correct_answer: G is on the median from A (to (b + c, d)), from B (to (c, d)), and from C (to (b, 0)), so the medians meet at G.
questions.required_method: Find the midpoint of each side, then show G is two-thirds of the way from each vertex to the opposite midpoint (or on each median line).
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: the three midpoints (b + c, d), (c, d), (b, 0); for each median, G = vertex + ⅔(midpoint - vertex): A + ⅔((b + c, d) - A) = G; B + ⅔((c, d) - (2b, 0)) = G; C + ⅔((b, 0) - (2c, 2d)) = G. Alternative: show G satisfies each median's equation. Invalid: checking one triangle with numbers.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, medians BE and CF meet at G. Let H and K be the midpoints of BG and CG. Prove that BG = 2GE. Then explain why the third median also passes through G.
questions.prompt_markup: In triangle ABC, medians BE and CF meet at G. Let H and K be the midpoints of BG and CG. Prove that BG = 2GE. Then explain why the third median also passes through G.
questions.correct_answer: BG = 2GE; the same argument for medians AD and BE gives the point that is two-thirds along BE, which is G, so AD passes through G.
questions.required_method: Use the midsegment theorem in triangles ABC and GBC to show FEKH is a parallelogram, then its diagonals.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: FE ∥ BC and FE = ½BC (midsegment in △ABC); HK ∥ BC and HK = ½BC (midsegment in △GBC); so FEKH is a parallelogram; its diagonals bisect each other, so HG = GE; with BH = HG, BG = 2GE; any two medians meet at the point two-thirds along each, so all three share it.
